title: GP Consult Template 'Back' text and chevron have poor contrast
kind_reason: The report marks this ticket 'Partially Fixed' after a fix attempt, meaning the defect persisted through a retest.
context: The Back label and chevron in the GP Consult Template header are dark on a dark blue background, making the control difficult to see. A fix was partially applied but the Back text and chevron have not been fully corrected; the outstanding elements have not yet passed the acceptance criteria for normal, hover, and focused states. The email confirms this ticket is about the low-contrast Back text and chevron only, not about saving states.
expected: Both the Back text and chevron are white, clearly legible, and visually consistent in normal, hover, and focused states.

title: Transcription service interruption silently stops recording mid-consultation; no persistent alert, no auto-reconnect
kind_reason: The ticket was reported fixed by Minh but the 12 October manual retest (Wi-Fi off for 60 seconds mid-recording) failed: no persistent alert appeared, only a transient toast, confirming the defect persists.
context: On 12 October, with Wi-Fi switched off for 60 seconds during a live recording, no centre-screen modal appeared. The only indication was a transient 'Connection failed: timeout' toast at the top right; recording stopped silently with the green mic still showing. The alert must be triggered client-side (websocket close or timeout), not by a server message, so it fires identically for a lost internet connection and for a transcription service outage. The service-outage case (transcription service stopped server-side for ≥30 seconds) has not yet been demonstrated by Minh with screenshots. The original 7 October event saw ~111 seconds of consultation audio lost without any persistent on-screen indication.
expected: A non-dismissable centre-screen modal reading 'RECORDING HAS STOPPED' appears within a few seconds of any connection loss, showing the time lost, a live 'Not recorded for' counter, a Resume recording primary action, and an audible alert; detection is client-side so it fires for both internet loss and service outage.

title: Resuming after an interruption discards the pre-interruption recording; saved session holds only the post-resume segment
kind_reason: The ticket was reported fixed by Minh; the Wi-Fi-loss retest on 12 October passed, but the same data-loss behaviour for a server-side service interruption has not yet been verified, so the defect is not fully closed.
context: The Wi-Fi-loss variant was verified on 12 October: pre-interruption content was retained after resuming via the green mic. Two cases remain untested: (1) a transcription-service-side interruption of ≥30 seconds — Minh must stop the service, resume, and provide screenshots showing audio, annotated transcript, Summary, and SNOMED codes contain content from both sides of the gap; (2) the clinician never resumes — the partial session up to the drop must be saved. The original 7 October failure saw ~6 minutes of pre-interruption audio and transcript entirely absent from the saved session with no indication to the clinician.
expected: Pre-interruption audio and transcript are retained and joined with post-resume content in the saved session (with a gap marker per JMD-07OCT-03), for both internet-loss and service-outage interruptions; if the clinician never resumes, the partial session up to the drop is saved.
report_status: Partially Verified – Service-Interruption Case and No-Resume Case Pending

title: Resumed transcript is appended straight after the cut-off with no gap marker
kind_reason: This ticket was first raised on 7 October 2026 and has not been reported as fixed or retested.
context: After a recording interruption and resume, new live transcript text followed directly after the mid-sentence cut-off with no indication that part of the consultation was not captured. The transcript therefore reads as continuous when it is not. The gap marker must appear in the live transcript, the annotated transcript, and the Summary, with correct start and end times for each interruption.
expected: A visible marker (e.g. '[Recording interrupted HH:MM:SS–HH:MM:SS – content not captured]') is inserted at the correct position in the live transcript, annotated transcript, and Summary for every interruption; multiple interruptions in one session are each marked.

title: Annotated transcript copy icon does not copy the transcript
kind_reason: This ticket was first raised on 7 October 2026 and has not been reported as fixed or retested.
context: The copy icon in the Transcription panel header does not copy the annotated transcript to the clipboard. The copy icon at the bottom of the Summary column works correctly and shows 'Copied!', but the transcript panel icon does nothing observable.
expected: Clicking the copy icon above the Transcription panel copies the full annotated transcript (all time blocks with Doctor/Patient labels) to the clipboard and shows a 'Copied!' confirmation.

title: Single '00:00:00 – 00:05:00' block label shown for a 9:25 recording
kind_reason: The same block-boundary labelling defect recurred on 12 October in a new form (one label repeated six times, now with a BST suffix), reported as JMD-12OCT-02, confirming the underlying fault was not fixed.
context: On 7 October, a 9:25 recording showed only one block label (00:00:00–00:05:00) despite the transcript content running to the end of the consultation. On 12 October the same defect appeared differently: six blocks all carrying the identical label '09:44:18 BST – 09:49:18 BST' for an 8:06 recording (JMD-12OCT-02). The block-boundary logic should be investigated together with JMD-12OCT-01 and JMD-12OCT-02.
expected: Block labels reflect the actual time ranges covered by each block, are unique and contiguous, together cover the full recording length, and match the recording start time.

title: Session activity timestamps use UTC-6 and now carry a misleading BST label; Encounter Date and Session activity disagree by 7 hours
kind_reason: A fix was attempted and the Encounter Date was corrected, but the 12 October retest showed Session activity still displays the UTC-6 value, now with an incorrect BST label, so the defect persists in a worse form.
context: On 12 October (session uk_abe9011f162d4869b84f6063e27c7384, viewed from a UTC+7 browser), the Encounter Date correctly shows 09:44:18 BST, but Session activity shows the same session-creation event as 02:44:18 BST — still the UTC-6 value, now carrying a BST label it does not deserve. The two panels disagree by 7 hours while both claim to be BST, which is an audit-trail integrity problem. Severity was raised from P3 to P2 for this reason. The automatic GMT/BST switch can only be verified after the clocks change on 25 October.
expected: Session activity is converted to Europe/London time (BST/GMT) in the same way as the Encounter Date; both panels show the same time for the same event, carry the correct zone label (BST or GMT), and are independent of the viewer's browser time zone.

title: SNOMED-CT Coder Re-code ignores clinician edits saved to the Summary
kind_reason: This ticket was first raised on 7 October 2026 and has not been reported as fixed or retested.
context: After a clinician added 'Statin Initiation: On atorvastatin' to the Procedure section of the Summary and saved it, clicking Re-code returned 10 concepts with no statin or atorvastatin concept. Re-code appears to use the original unedited Summary rather than the latest saved version. Additionally, the edited line appeared twice in the Summary (the second marked '[corrected]'), and it is unconfirmed whether this duplication is intentional.
expected: Re-code always uses the latest saved version of the Summary including clinician edits; newly added conditions, medications, and procedures appear in the output; removed items no longer appear; the coded Summary version is recorded in the audit trail; and an edited line appears once only.

title: Exit survey Q1 'What drove the correction' options have no borders and do not look selectable
kind_reason: This ticket was first raised on 7 October 2026 and has not been reported as fixed or retested.
context: In the exit survey Q1 follow-up ('What drove the correction required? Select all that apply'), options such as Misattribution, Wrong section, Too verbose, and Style or phrasing appear as plain unstyled text in their unselected state; only selected options become filled blue pills. Users may not realise the options are clickable or that multiple selections are possible. The proposed exit survey design (v1) shows each option as a bordered pill with an icon.
expected: Every Q1 follow-up option has a visible border in its unselected state, a clearly distinct filled style when selected, visible hover and keyboard-focus states, and 'Other (please specify)' follows the same style; multi-select works correctly.

title: Annotated transcript silently omits a 1 min 47 s segment (3:33–5:20) that was recorded and transcribed live
kind_reason: This ticket was first identified during the 12 October automated run and has not been reported as fixed or retested.
context: In session uk_abe9011f162d4869b84f6063e27c7384 (Primock D1C01, 12 October), recording ran uninterrupted for 458 seconds with no interruption notification. The saved audio contains speech throughout 3:33–5:20 (confirmed by playback) and the live transcript contained this stretch (Chinese takeaway, asthma, occupation, household contacts). The annotated transcript omits it entirely: the first block ends mid-sentence at 'Patient: Yeah, so I' and the next block starts at 'Doctor: Two children. Is that right', with no marker, so the transcript reads as continuous. The omission falls at the 5-minute block boundary. The missing content propagates: the Summary contains no past history of asthma, no inhaler use, no occupation, and no household contacts; the SNOMED-CT Coder has no asthma concept (195967001). The clinician receives no indication at any stage that content is missing. The email identifies this as the highest priority and states the evaluation cannot resume until it is understood. It should be investigated together with JMD-12OCT-02 and JMD-07OCT-05 as they share the same block-boundary logic.
expected: Every segment transcribed live appears in the annotated transcript; if a segment cannot be speaker-labelled it is inserted unannotated with a visible marker rather than dropped; the Summary and SNOMED codes are not generated from a transcript with an unmarked gap, and if a gap is unavoidable the clinician is informed before outputs are presented.

title: Transcript block label '09:44:18 – 09:49:18 BST' repeated six times; blocks not labelled with their own time ranges
kind_reason: The report explicitly states this extends JMD-07OCT-05 (one incorrect label for a 9:25 recording), identifying it as the same block-boundary labelling defect returning in a new form.
context: In session uk_abe9011f162d4869b84f6063e27c7384 (12 October, 8:06 recording), all six annotated transcript blocks carry the identical label '09:44:18 BST – 09:49:18 BST'. This label equals the session creation time (Encounter Date) plus five minutes, not the actual time range of each block. The BST suffix is new since 7 October. The same block-boundary logic is implicated in JMD-12OCT-01 (content dropped at the 5-minute boundary) and JMD-07OCT-05, and the email asks that all three be investigated together.
expected: Each block is labelled with its own unique start and end time in UK time with the correct zone suffix (BST/GMT); consecutive block labels are contiguous and together cover the full recording length, consistent with the recording start time.

title: Initial page load of jarvismd-trial.xycare.co.uk takes about 75 seconds on every browser and network tested
kind_reason: This ticket was first identified during manual testing on 12 October 2026 and has not been reported as fixed or retested.
context: On 12 October, the first load of jarvismd-trial.xycare.co.uk took approximately 75 seconds to display, reproduced across multiple browsers and on both Wi-Fi and 5G connections, ruling out a single-device or single-network cause. A clinician opening the application at the start of a surgery would wait over a minute before the first patient could be started. The report marks this as must fix before witness testing.
expected: Initial cold load completes within 5 seconds on a normal broadband or 5G connection; subsequent navigation within 2 seconds; if a backend component has a cold start it is kept warm or the user is shown a progress state rather than a blank page.
